clue.text: Unpremeditated retreat of certain vessels

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word for the vessels is read backwards

parts.note: pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A naval squadron pulls back without any planning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat of' turns PANS round to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap decision or election is one made suddenly, without forethought.

clue.text: Leningrad's bizarre wading bird

indicators.note: bizarre means strange or distorted, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: here the S of the possessive counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A strange bird has been spotted wading near the old Soviet city.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually the possessive S is part of the anagram fodder: all ten letters of LENINGRADS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The sanderling is a small sandpiper that runs along the tideline, a typical shore wader.

clue.text: A source of irritation at the end of March

parts.note: an itch is something that irritates the skin

explanation.surface: Something annoying crops up as March draws to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the letter whose name is spelt as the answer, H, stands at the end of the word March.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spelt-out name of the letter H, the final letter of the word March.

clue.text: Foreign articles not initially selected for wear in Bavaria

parts.note: le is the French word for 'the'
der is the German word for 'the'

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for selected is dropped

parts.note: chosen means selected

explanation.surface: Imported goods, the ones nobody picked first, end up as clothing in southern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign articles' supplies two pieces: French LE and German DER. 'not initially' removes the C from CHOSEN, leaving HOSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather shorts with braces are the traditional dress of Bavaria, the southern German state.

clue.text: Rising musical reputation tending to emerge

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the whole run of pieces is turned backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
a name is a reputation, as in making a name for oneself

explanation.surface: A stage show's growing fame is starting to show itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns the whole run EVITA + NAME upward, giving EMANATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emanative issues or flows out, so it tends to come forth or emerge.

clue.text: Constable's supporter, a sly type out West

indicators.note: out means the letter for West is taken away

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, crafty person

explanation.surface: A policeman's backer turns out to be a cunning fellow from the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' looks like a policeman, but it is John Constable the painter, whose canvas rests on the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand that holds a painter's canvas, so it supports the artist Constable's work.

clue.text: Rider of hollow-eyed appearance

definitions.meaning: H. Rider ... was the author of King Solomon's Mines

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' is the novelist's middle name, the one he was known by, so his surname is the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian adventure novelist was Henry Rider Haggard; as an adjective the word means gaunt and worn.

clue.text: African state's grounds for supporting extremists in Westminster

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supporting another sits beneath it
in places the extremes of the alphabet inside the postcode

parts.note: SW1, written here as SWI, is the London postcode for Westminster
A and Z are the extreme letters of the alphabet
land means grounds or an estate

explanation.surface: A nation in Africa provides grounds for backing the radicals in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' is not political: A and Z are the alphabet's extremes. SW1 is the Westminster postcode, its 1 read as I; 'in' and 'supporting' (beneath, in a down clue) place the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaziland, now Eswatini, is a small kingdom in southern Africa.

clue.text: Negative voters' narrow margin of victory, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a horse that wins by a nose wins by the narrowest margin

explanation.surface: Those voting against won by only a whisker, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals the homophone: NOSE, as in winning by a nose, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a parliamentary division those voting against a motion are called the noes.

clue.text: Ornament, notice, in canopy that's put up

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the assembled letters are read upwards
in places the notice inside the canopy

parts.note: a hood is a canopy or covering
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A decoration and a notice are fixed into an awning that has been erected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the notice inside the canopy, giving HADOOD, which 'put up' reads upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodah is an informal word for a gadget or trinket whose name escapes you, such as a decorative knick-knack.

clue.text: Current cricket side welcomed by old province's citizens

indicators.note: to be welcomed by is to be taken in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: Natal was a former province of South Africa; with the possessive S it gives NATALS
I is the symbol for electric current
the on side is one half of a cricket field, also called leg side

explanation.surface: A cricket team on tour is greeted warmly by the people of a former province.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal was a South African province until 1994. In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side; 'welcomed by' puts current and side inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationals are citizens of a particular country.

clue.text: For example, Euphrosyne's beauty of movement

definitions.meaning: Euphrosyne is one of the three ... of Greek myth, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Euphrosyne is read as 'is': Euphrosyne is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The three Graces of myth were Euphrosyne, Aglaia and Thalia; the word also means elegance in movement.

clue.text: This insectivore can hide as it moves

indicators.note: as the letters move about they form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A spiny ant-eater can hide by burrowing as it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it moves' rearranges CANHIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an Australian egg-laying mammal that feeds on ants and termites.

clue.text: Girl overwhelmed by film director's introduction

indicators.note: being overwhelmed by something means being covered by it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: David Lean directed Lawrence of Arabia
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A young actress is swamped by the opening a famous filmmaker gives her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film director' is David Lean, of Lawrence of Arabia; 'overwhelmed by' puts the girl inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead-in is an introductory passage or remark that opens a programme or piece.

clue.text: Component of long books an artist first abridged?

indicators.note: first puts the shortened painter ahead of the other pieces
abridged means shortened, so the painter's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Ingres was a French neoclassical painter
to die for something is to long for it
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Part of a lengthy set of volumes on a painter was the first thing cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' drops the painter's last letter, and 'first' puts him before the rest. 'long' is the verb, as in dying for something.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one element or constituent of a mixture.

clue.text: Simulate a channel for conveying raucous mirth

definitions.text: Simulate a channel for conveying raucous mirth

parts.words: Simulate a channel for conveying raucous mirth
parts.note: read literally, imitate a gurgling gutter; really, the idiom for guffawing loudly and coarsely

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom means to laugh loudly and coarsely, like water gurgling noisily down a drain; the clue pretends the drain is a channel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a loud, coarse laugh, compared to the gurgle of water going down a plughole.

clue.text: Innocent comedian involved in East End blood sport?

indicators.note: being involved in something means being inside it, so these letters are placed within

parts.note: hunting said in a Cockney East End accent drops its H
a wit is a witty person or comic

explanation.surface: A comic, innocently, gets caught up in a cruel sport in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: East End Londoners (Cockneys) famously drop their H's, so the blood sport loses its first letter; 'involved in' puts the comedian inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwitting means not knowing, so an unwitting party is innocent of what is going on.

clue.text: Note range of colours round posh coat ornament

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: round means the range of colours goes around the letter for posh

parts.note: a palette is the range of colours a painter uses
U means upper-class, as opposed to non-U

explanation.surface: A dress coat's decoration comes in a smart selection of shades.
explanation.walkthrough: PALETTE goes round U, the British label for upper-class usage, after the note E.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is the ornamental shoulder piece on a military coat.

clue.text: Breaking law, recent agenda reveals record of criminals

indicators.note: breaking the words up lets their letters be rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A recent agenda shows the law being broken, with offenders on file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges LAW and RECENT AGENDA. The Newgate Calendar was a famous series of accounts of criminals held at London's Newgate Prison.
explanation.definitionFit: This eighteenth- and nineteenth-century publication chronicled the crimes of notorious prisoners of Newgate.

clue.text: Valerian, perhaps? A heartlessly lethal scoundrel, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound-alike, so the spoken words stand for the entry

parts.note: A, then lethal without its inner letters (LL), then heel meaning a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy is said to be a cold-hearted villain's handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the middle out of lethal, leaving LL; A + LL + HEEL is said aloud ('we hear') as the plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: All-heal is an old name for several medicinal plants, valerian among them; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Hire European device to protect front of machine

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of the word

parts.note: a ploy is a device or stratagem

explanation.surface: Take on a Continental gadget to shield the front of the machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' puts PLOY round M, the first letter of machine ('front of'), after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ someone is to hire them to work for you.

clue.text: Unemotional type originally employed in stable

indicators.note: employed in means used inside, so the letter goes within the other word

parts.note: solid means firm or stable

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dour character was once on the payroll at a racing stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unemotional type' looks like the definition, but 'type' gives T ('originally'), which is put inside SOLID ('employed in').
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive, showing little emotion.

clue.text: Crazy set-up supported by Pythias's friend

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means turned upwards

parts.note: mad means crazy
on means resting on top of, so the first piece is supported by the second

explanation.surface: A mad scheme is backed by a loyal companion from Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' turns the crazy word upward to give DAM. Damon and Pythias are the classical byword for devoted friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Damon offered his life as surety for his friend Pythias.

clue.text: Gain information from some subject to smacking?

definitions.text: Gain information from some subject to smacking?

parts.words: Gain information from some subject to smacking?
parts.note: seems to be about beating someone for information; really the subjects smacked are lips, watched to follow speech

explanation.walkthrough: The 'some subject to smacking' are lips, which can be smacked; watching them move lets a deaf person follow speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To understand speech by watching the movements of a speaker's mouth.

clue.text: Aristocratic type

definitions.meaning: a size of typewriter type, twelve characters to the inch

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a typewriter typeface, smaller than pica.
explanation.definitionFit: The select few form the upper crust; it is also a small typewriter typeface.

clue.text: Small island in Martin Chuzzlewit

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the title words

explanation.surface: A tiny isle features in a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles MartIN CHuzzlewit. An inch is a Scottish word for a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: Inch, from Gaelic innis, is a Scottish term for a small island, as in Inchcolm.

clue.text: Artless like 10, lacking the ultimate in craft

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: 10 across is nationals, citizens; native means belonging by birth, like them

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An unsophisticated local is short of skill at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: NATIVE (like the citizens of 10) loses T, the last letter of craft ('the ultimate in').
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and unsophisticated, lacking guile.

clue.text: English novice returns to measure fallen stone

parts.note: to mete is to measure out

indicators.note: returns means the word for a novice is read backwards

parts.note: a tiro is a beginner

explanation.surface: An English beginner goes back to weighing a rock that has dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the novice into ORIT; tiro is a crossword favourite for a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorite is a stone from space that has fallen to Earth.

clue.text: Scot, possibly, turned on light with hesitation

parts.note: high means intoxicated, turned on by drugs
to light is to alight or land
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Switching on a lamp, the man paused before speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned on' is not an anagram signal: it means stoned, HIGH. 'light' is the verb to alight, LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highlander comes from the Scottish Highlands, so is an example of a Scot.

clue.text: Fingered material for a fedora

definitions.meaning: touched with the fingers, the past tense of feel
the fabric a soft brimmed hat is made from

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both the past tense of 'feel' and a pressed wool fabric used for hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is the past of feel, so fingered; it is also the matted fabric fedoras are made from.
